newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gabon president said angered by French probe.
newsitem.headline: Gabon president said angered by French probe.

text.p: Gabonese President Omar Bongo has telephoned French President Jacques Chirac to voice anger at a Paris judge's investigation into the Elf Aquitaine oil company's activities in the west African state, sources close to the case said on Monday.
The Foreign Ministry played down a report on Monday that relations with Gabon were in crisis because of investigating magistrate Eva Joly's probe.
But the sources told Reuters Bongo had telephoned Chirac 10 days ago, after first sending him a letter of protest, and "was really furious".

The newspaper Le Monde said Elf chairman Philippe Jaffre was flying to Libreville on Monday to try to calm Bongo's anger over the freezing of a Swiss bank account on Joly's order and head off a diplomatic crisis.
It said the veteran Gabonese leader had threatened Chirac with "economic sanctions" and had also sent an angry letter to Jaffre, who heads the main foreign oil firm operating in Gabon.
Elf declined comment, saying it never disclosed Jaffre's movements.
Joly has been investigating alleged fraud at Elf while former French railways chief Loic Le Floch-Prigent was chairman in 1988-93, involving the payment of alleged covert commissions.

The chairman of Elf's Gabon subsidiary, Andre Tarallo, was placed under judicial investigation last Friday for receiving the proceeds of misuse of corporate funds in the probe and freed on 10 million francs ($1.8 million) bail, justice sources said.

Chirac's office said it would not comment on a matter which was under judicial investigation, but a Foreign Ministry spokesman, Yves Doutriaux, played down talk of a crisis in relations, noting that Gabon had denied it.

"We noted that after the publication of a press article last week, the Gabonese authorities published a very clear denial, stating that relations between France and Gabon were excellent," he told a briefing.
